results.reason: The response identifies the Varga acquisition as a Change of Control that needs Crestline's prior written consent under DA 15.4. It says Part 3.5 wrongly lists the agreement as notice-only. It explains the resulting termination right, the termination fee, and the inaccurate SPA 3.5 representation.

Issue 2 explains that Section 14.2, read with the 'Qualified Transferee' definition, allows assignment without consent to any lab or diagnostic distributor in the Territory. It notes there is no exclusion for competitors or their affiliates.

Issue 3 explains that First Amendment Section 3.1 leaves only the Section 9 carve-out and drops the Section 10 and 11 carve-outs. It states that the amendment controls under DA 17.5, so claims against Crestline are now capped.
The response states that the original 12.3 excluded breaches of Sections 9 and 10 and indemnification obligations under Section 11.
The response states that the cap is the amounts paid or payable to Supplier in the 12 months preceding the claim.
The response is a memo with separate issues. Each issue gives the document and section, why it matters for Halvorsen, and a recommended fix.
The response concludes that consent is required and says the notice-only description is wrong.
The response expressly says the original carve-outs no longer apply unless a further amendment is signed.
